title: Smith-Midland Producing over $1M in Utility Vaults for Virginia Data Center
summary: MIDLAND, VA – December 16, 2025 – Smith-Midland Corporation (NASDAQ: SMID) announced today that production is underway on underground precast utility vaults ...
body_text: Smith-Midland Producing over $1M in Utility Vaults for Virginia Data Center December 22, 2025 | Utility Products MIDLAND, VA – December 16, 2025 – Smith-Midland Corporation (NASDAQ: SMID) announced today that production is underway on underground precast utility vaults and manholes for a new data center in Mineral, VA. The contract, valued at more than $1 million, is being produced at Smith-Midland’s Virginia precast plant, with all units scheduled for delivery by the beginning of 2026. The precast vaults will house the facility’s electrical and telecom lines, delivering essential underground infrastructure for reliable power and connectivity. Smith-Midland is also providing the accompanying cast-iron access frames and covers, including a large 48-inch unit designed for heavy-duty performance. “Precast utility structures like these allow data centers and other facilities to accelerate construction schedules while ensuring reliable, long-term performance,” said Ashley Smith, President and CEO of Smith-Midland. “This project reflects the strong demand we are experiencing for resilient infrastructure solutions and aligns with our strategic plan to expand our presence in high-growth sectors such as data centers and utilities. By investing in advanced precast technologies and delivering products that combine quality craftsmanship, durability and value, we continue to create opportunities for our stakeholders while reinforcing Smith-Midland’s reputation as an industry leader.” Smith-Midland manufactures a wide range of standard utility vaults, designed to be the most economical choice for underground infrastructure. Readily available in many shapes and sizes, each piece is built to uniform quality standards, with 5,000 psi concrete and H-20 highway traffic load ratings. Custom designs are also available for specialized applications, ensuring flexibility for both standard and mission-critical projects like data centers. About Smith-Midland Corporation Smith-Midland develops, manufactures, licenses, rents, and sells a broad array of precast concrete products for use primarily in the construction, transportation, and utility industries. Smith-Midland Corporation has three manufacturing facilities in: Midland, VA, Reidsville, NC, and Columbia, SC, and a J-J Hooks® Safety Barrier rental firm, Concrete Safety Systems . Easi-Set Worldwide, a wholly owned subsidiary of Smith-Midland Corporation, licenses the production and sale of Easi-Set products, including J-J Hooks and SlenderWall®, and provides diversification opportunities to the precast industry worldwide. For more information, please call (540) 439-3266 or visit www.smithmidland.com . title: The Second Decoupling: Bringing Compute to the Power
summary: by Dip Patel, CTO For decades, we’ve built a cloud optimized for humans — not machines. That cloud was about... Read more »
body_text: by Dip Patel , CTO For decades, we’ve built a cloud optimized for humans — not machines. That cloud was about people: real-time transactions, video streaming, milliseconds of ping, and proximity. This has driven a huge premium in “tier-1” cities for data center space, which in turn causes havoc to the local electrical grid, water table, and environment. The AI cloud is different. It’s about power, scale, and physics. It’s far easier to move information than it is to move power. The first digital decoupling: When COVID hit, the internet quietly rewired the physical world. Using the internet, we stopped moving people to offices, and the world was handled on Zoom. Traffic disappeared. The skies cleared. Even whales returned to the coast. The earth was healing. That was the first great digital decoupling — the moment we learned that work, learning, and creativity didn’t have to orbit the city center. The next decoupling will be data centers. And, just like companies that ignored hybrid work, those that ignore this shift will go extinct. Over the last six weeks, I’ve met the people trying to scale everything that fuels AI: Power. People. Pipes. I learned that a lot of them are still stuck in the real estate mindset that defined the last cloud. They’re chasing Tier-1 metros, zoning maps, and carrier hotels (internet exchange buildings), because that’s where the internet used to live. That cloud was built for serving websites and YouTube. But the AI cloud doesn’t need to live there. It doesn’t chase clicks or milliseconds. It chases megawatts. We’ve crossed into a new paradigm — one where companies built for location are now facing a world that needs power. Companies that have built their entire DNA tending to horses (location) are now staring at a car (power). In the traditional cloud, every millisecond of ping mattered. You wanted to be as close as possible to Internet exchange points (Ashburn, Dallas, Columbus). In the AI cloud, proximity takes on a new meaning. What matters now is how fast GPUs talk to each other inside the same building — not across the map. They communicate at 3,200 Gbps across GPU nodes and 1.8 Tbps within a single motherboard. Outside of the building? Latency is a lot less sensitive. Training workloads run for days or weeks. A few milliseconds (ms) make no difference. Inference workloads are more mixed: only 10–20% demand sub-10 ms latency for real-time use cases such as robotics or autonomous systems. The rest? They’re perfectly fine in the 10–100 ms range. For every extra ms in latency, you can move a building 150 miles from a tier-1 city, where land, power, and permitting are easier. Building new transmission is nearly impossible. Building new fiber is trivial. POWER (Transmission) INFORMATION (Fiber) COST/km $2–6M $25–60K TIMELINE 5–10 years <1 year REGULATION FERC + State + NEPA DOT + County RISK Grid Instability Minimal FLEXIBILITY Fixed Infinite For decades, we brought power to the cities, but that was low-power compute. Now it’s time to bring cities of compute to the power. This is the second decoupling , and the divide will define the next decade. Companies still optimizing around Tier-1 real estate are building for the past. The future doesn’t belong to whoever’s closest to an exchange point. It belongs to whoever’s closest to a substation. Because in the AI era, it’s easier to move bits than electrons. Learn more about Soluna visit → https://www.solunacomputing.com/

title: How to Choose Desk Booking Software: 6 Top Picks
summary: Selecting a desk booking tool? Our guide covers key features like Teams integration, analytics, and mobile access to help you decide. Find the right software now.
body_text: The morning scramble for a good desk is more than just an annoyance—it's a productivity killer. In a hybrid model, this daily game of musical chairs creates stress and wastes valuable time. A desk booking tool solves this by letting everyone reserve their spot in advance. But the real challenge isn't just finding a tool, it's finding the right one. So, how to choose a hot desking or desk booking software for my office that actually works for your team? We’ll show you what features matter most to make your office days intentional and productive. Key Takeaways Choose software that lives where your team works : To ensure your team actually uses the new tool, select one that integrates directly into the platforms they use every day, like Slack or Microsoft Teams. This removes friction and makes booking a desk a natural part of their workflow. Turn office data into cost savings : A good desk booking tool provides clear analytics on how your space is used. Leverage this data to make informed decisions about your office layout and real estate needs, preventing you from paying for underutilized space. Match features to your real problems : Before looking at price, list your must-have features, like automated check-ins or calendar integration. This allows you to evaluate tools based on the value they provide and ensures you invest in a solution that solves your specific challenges. What Exactly is a Desk Booking Tool? Let's cut through the jargon. At its core, a desk booking tool is a simple system that helps your team reserve a workspace before they come into the office. Think of it like booking a seat at a movie theater, but for your desk. Instead of wandering around looking for a free spot or showing up to find the office is already at capacity, your employees can see what's available and claim their space ahead of time. This simple act of planning removes a ton of friction from the hybrid work model, making office days more intentional and productive for everyone involved. It’s the key to managing a flexible space without the chaos. Hot Desking vs. Desk Hoteling: What's the Difference? You've probably heard these terms used interchangeably, but they describe two different approaches to flexible seating. Think of hot desking as a "first-come, first-served" system where employees grab any open desk when they arrive. It’s spontaneous but can lead to uncertainty. Desk hoteling, on the other hand, is more structured. It requires employees to reserve a specific desk in advance for a set period, just like booking a hotel room. This guarantees everyone a spot and helps office managers anticipate who's coming in and how the space will be used on any given day. While a booking tool can support both models, it’s the backbone of an effective desk hoteling system. A good hot desk booking system eliminates the guesswork by allowing your team to see availability and book their spot directly within tools they already use, like Slack or Microsoft Teams. This simple reservation process turns a potentially chaotic office into a well-organized and predictable workspace. It ensures your team can focus on their work from the moment they walk in, not on finding a place to do it. How Desk Booking Software Simplifies Your Day A desk booking tool, sometimes called hot desking software , lets employees pick a desk before they even leave the house. Through a simple app—often one that works right within Slack or Teams—they can see a schedule, choose a day they want to come in, and reserve a specific desk. This helps everyone plan their on-site and remote days with more confidence. For office managers, it provides a clear picture of who is coming in and when, which helps with everything from managing capacity to stocking the right amount of coffee. It’s all about bringing predictability and ease to a flexible work environment, which ultimately improves employee satisfaction and makes the office run more smoothly. Need a Desk? Find One in Seconds Once you’re in the office, the best desk booking tools don't just stop at the reservation. Many platforms include a live map of the office floor plan, so you can instantly see which desks are free, booked, or currently in use. This is a lifesaver when you need to find a quiet corner for a last-minute call or want to sit near a specific teammate. Some tools even have wayfinding features that help you navigate the office and easily find your reserved desk or locate meeting rooms . It takes the guesswork out of finding your spot, so your team can settle in and get to work faster. Which Industries Benefit Most from Desk Booking? While any company with a hybrid model can see gains, desk booking tools are especially transformative for industries like tech, consulting, and financial services. In these fields, employees are often on the move—visiting clients, attending conferences, or working on project-based teams. A dedicated desk for every person simply doesn't make sense. By implementing a hot desking system , these organizations can optimize their expensive office real estate and make data-driven decisions about their space needs. More importantly, it empowers employees to book a desk only when they need one, turning the office into a purposeful hub for collaboration rather than a daily requirement. This shift not only cuts costs but also improves the employee experience by giving them the autonomy to work where they're most effective. What Should You Look For in a Desk Booking Tool? Not all desk booking tools are created equal. When you start comparing options, you'll see a wide range of features, from basic booking calendars to complex workplace management suites. The key is to find a tool that solves your specific problems without adding unnecessary complexity for your team. A clunky tool that no one uses is worse than no tool at all. The best systems are the ones that fit so seamlessly into your team's daily routine that they barely notice they're using something new. Think about your company culture and your existing tech stack. Do your employees live in Slack or Teams? Then a tool that integrates directly with those platforms will see much higher adoption than one that requires a separate login and app. Focus on features that make life easier for both employees and the people managing the office. Below are the non-negotiable features you should look for. Seamless Booking on Any Device In a hybrid world, planning is everything. Your team needs to be able to book a desk from anywhere, whether they’re on their laptop at home or on their phone during their morning commute. A good hot desk booking system should be accessible on any device. This flexibility allows employees to coordinate their office days with colleagues and plan their week with confidence. If booking a desk feels like a chore, people will simply stop doing it. Look for a tool with a clean, intuitive interface that works just as well on a mobile browser as it does on a desktop. Does It Integrate with Your Calendar and HR Tools? The last thing you want is another piece of software that operates in a silo. A great desk booking tool should integrate with the systems you already use every day. Calendar integrations, for example, can automatically add desk bookings to an employee's schedule, making it easy to see who will be in the office and when. Connections with HR tools can automate user management, so new hires are added and departing employees are removed without any manual work. When you explore integrations , you'll find that the most effective tools are those that become a natural part of your existing workflow. Get Smart Insights with Workplace Analytics How do you know if your office space is actually working for your team? Guessing can be expensive. The right desk booking tool gives you the data to make informed decisions. Look for a platform with a strong analytics dashboard that shows you booking trends, peak usage days, and which desks or areas are most popular. This information is invaluable for optimizing your office layout, deciding on future real estate needs, and ensuring you’re not paying for space you don’t need. Good hybrid work software turns raw data into clear, actionable insights. Automate Check-Ins and Set Custom Booking Rules Every office has its own unique needs and policies. Your desk booking tool should be flexible enough to accommodate them. Look for features that let you set custom rules, like how far in advance someone can book a desk or which teams can book in specific "neighborhoods." Automated check-ins are also a huge help. They can automatically release a booked desk if an employee doesn't show up, preventing "ghost bookings" and freeing up space for others. This kind of flex office software helps you manage the office efficiently without needing a dedicated person to police the seating chart. Advanced Features to Consider Once you've covered the essentials like easy booking and analytics, you can start looking at features that take your office management to the next level. These advanced capabilities are designed to solve more specific challenges, from welcoming visitors to making your office smarter and more responsive. While not every company will need these on day one, they are worth considering as you think about your long-term workplace strategy. They can help you create a truly seamless and efficient office experience for everyone, not just your full-time employees. Visitor Management and Kiosk Access Your office isn't just for your team; it's also a space for clients, partners, and interview candidates. A robust desk booking tool should include features for visitor management , allowing you to pre-register guests and assign them a temporary workspace. This creates a professional and welcoming experience from the moment they arrive. Some systems also offer kiosk access, which allows both employees and visitors to check in on a tablet at the front desk. This streamlines the arrival process, reduces the burden on your reception staff, and helps you keep an accurate record of who is in the building at all times. Hardware and AI Integration The smartest desk booking tools use technology to make your office more efficient without you having to lift a finger. Look for AI-powered features that can suggest the best desk for an employee based on their team's location or their personal preferences. These systems can also use data to predict future space needs , helping you make smarter real estate decisions. Some platforms can even integrate with hardware like desk sensors that automatically detect when a space is occupied, freeing up "no-show" bookings in real-time. This ensures every square foot of your office is used effectively, saving energy and reducing costs. Data Privacy and Security Considerations Desk booking software, by its nature, collects data about your employees' schedules and their location within the office. Because of this, data privacy and security can't be an afterthought. Any tool you consider must be compliant with privacy regulations like GDPR and have clear policies on how it handles sensitive information. A trustworthy platform will only collect the data that is absolutely necessary, give you control over who can access it, and store it securely using strong encryption. Before you commit to a tool, ask potential vendors about their security protocols and data handling practices to ensure your company and your employees are protected. The Best Desk Booking Software for Hybrid Workplaces Choosing the right desk booking tool can feel like a big decision, but it really comes down to how your team works. Each platform has its own strengths, whether it’s integrating with the software you already use, providing deep analytics, or offering a full suite of workplace tools. Think about your company’s biggest needs. Are you trying to get everyone to adopt a new system with minimal fuss? Do you need hard data to justify your office layout? Or are you looking for a single tool to manage everything from desks to visitors? To help you find the perfect fit, I’ve broken down six of the best desk booking tools on the market. We’ll look at what makes each one unique, who it’s best for, and what you can expect from its core features. This isn’t about finding the one "best" tool, but about finding the one that’s best for you . Let’s get into the specifics so you can make a choice that feels right for your team and your office. Understanding the Desk Booking Market The desk booking market has grown from simple reservation calendars into a sophisticated category of workplace management tools. At its heart, the purpose remains the same: to help your team reserve a workspace before they come into the office. This simple function is critical for making hybrid work models successful, as it removes the uncertainty and friction that can make office days feel chaotic. A key trend defining the market is the shift toward deep integration with the communication platforms teams already use daily. To ensure high adoption, leading solutions are built to work directly within Slack and Microsoft Teams, making booking a desk a natural part of the workflow. Beyond simple reservations, these tools are also becoming powerful data sources, providing clear analytics on office usage to help you make informed decisions about your real estate needs and create an office that truly serves your team. Officely: The Go-To for Slack and Teams Integration If your team communicates and collaborates primarily through Slack or Microsoft Teams, Officely is designed for you. Its biggest advantage is that it works inside the platforms your employees already have open all day. This eliminates the need to introduce and train everyone on a separate app, which is a huge win for adoption. You can manage your entire hot desk booking system without ever leaving your chat window. Officely’s features include everything from simple desk booking and real-time office maps to attendance analytics, making it a streamlined solution for hybrid teams that value simplicity and convenience. Deskbird: A Seamless Fit for the Microsoft Ecosystem For companies heavily invested in the Microsoft ecosystem, Deskbird is a standout option. It integrates smoothly with Microsoft Teams and Outlook, allowing employees to book desks directly from their calendars. This tight integration helps make desk booking a natural part of their daily planning process. According to People Managing People, Deskbird is one of the best tools for working with Microsoft products. With a 14-day free trial and pricing that starts at a low per-user cost, it’s an accessible option for businesses that want to add desk booking capabilities to their existing Microsoft toolkit. OfficeSpace: When You Need Deep, Enterprise-Level Analytics If you’re managing a large office or multiple locations, data is your best friend. OfficeSpace is built for companies that need detailed analytics to make smart decisions about their real estate. The software provides in-depth reports and visual "heat maps" that show exactly how your desks and meeting rooms are being used. This information is invaluable for understanding peak usage times, identifying underutilized areas, and planning for future needs. As OfficeSpace notes, these insights help companies "understand their office space better and make smart decisions," making it ideal for enterprise-level space optimization. Eden: More Than Just Desks, It's a Full Workplace Platform Eden is more than just a desk booking tool; it’s a comprehensive workplace management platform. It’s the right choice for companies looking for a single solution to handle desk reservations, meeting room scheduling, visitor management, and even internal ticketing. By bundling these functions together, Eden helps streamline office operations and reduce the number of different software tools your team has to manage. If you want one central hub for all things related to your physical workspace, Eden’s all-in-one approach is a powerful and efficient option. Robin: Designed to Maximize In-Office Collaboration Robin is designed to make time in the office more intentional and productive. It goes beyond simply reserving a desk by offering features that help employees connect and collaborate. Users can see who else is coming into the office and book desks near their teammates to work together on projects. The platform also includes tools for finding and booking available meeting rooms on the fly. For teams that see the office as a hub for collaboration rather than just a place to work, Robin’s focus on in-person productivity makes it a compelling choice. Envoy: A Great Choice for Managing Desks and Visitors Envoy is a versatile tool that excels at managing both employee desk bookings and visitor experiences. Its hot desk booking software provides interactive office maps that help employees find available desks and see where their colleagues are sitting. At the same time, its robust visitor management system streamlines the check-in process for guests, contractors, and interview candidates. This dual functionality makes Envoy a great fit for dynamic offices with a steady flow of both employees and visitors, ensuring a smooth and organized experience for everyone who walks through the door. The Unexpected Benefits of Desk Booking Software A desk booking tool might seem like just another piece of software, but it's one of the smartest investments a hybrid company can make. It goes beyond simply assigning seats; it fundamentally changes how your office operates for the better. From saving serious money on real estate to making your team genuinely happier to be in the office, the benefits are tangible. Let's look at the real perks you can expect when you find the right tool. Optimize Your Office Space and Reduce Costs Are you paying for a huge office that sits half-empty most of the week? You're not alone. A hot desk booking system helps you understand exactly how your space is being used—or not used. By allowing employees to reserve desks as needed, you ensure every square foot is working for you. Over time, the data you collect provides a clear picture of your actual needs. You might discover you can downsize your office, sublet a floor, or reconfigure the layout to better suit your team's habits, all of which translates directly into significant cost savings. Quantifying the ROI: Key Statistics The savings aren't just theoretical; the numbers back it up. With the right data, companies can often reduce the office space they need by 20-40% just by using it more efficiently. A good desk booking tool provides clear analytics on booking trends, peak usage days, and which areas are most popular. You can leverage this data to make informed decisions about your office layout and real estate needs, preventing you from paying for underutilized space. In fact, the money saved from this optimization can often pay for the software itself in just 12-18 months, turning your office from a fixed cost into a flexible, strategic asset. Create a Happier Team and Foster Collaboration The morning scramble for a good desk is a real source of stress for hybrid teams. A booking tool eliminates that anxiety. When employees know they have a guaranteed spot waiting for them, they can focus on their work, not their workspace. This simple act of giving them control and flexibility can make them more productive and happier. Plus, it makes collaboration intentional. Teams can easily see who’s in the office and book desks near each other, turning in-office days into valuable, connected time instead of a game of chance. Good hybrid work software makes this coordination seamless. Measuring the Impact on Employee Satisfaction The positive shift in office vibe is often something you can feel, but how do you actually measure it? The most direct way is to ask your team. Simple, anonymous pulse surveys are a great tool for this. Instead of just asking if they're "happy," get specific. Ask questions like, "How has the desk booking system changed your experience of coming into the office?" or "Do you find it easier to plan collaborative days with your team now?" Tracking these responses over time will give you clear data on the impact. When you give employees more control over their workday, satisfaction naturally follows. In fact, some reports show this kind of flexibility can improve workplace satisfaction by 30% or more. This isn't just about providing a desk; it's about using hybrid work software to create a better, less stressful environment. Plan Your Office Future with Real Data Guesswork has no place in your real estate strategy. A desk booking app gives you powerful insights into how your office actually functions. You can see which days are the busiest, which desks are the most popular, and which areas are consistently empty. This data is gold. With detailed reports and analytics, you can make informed decisions about the future of your workplace. Do you need more collaborative zones? Fewer individual desks? This information helps you build an office that truly serves your team's needs and allows you to manage a flex office with confidence, ensuring you're not wasting money on space that doesn't get used. How Much Do Desk Booking Tools Cost? Figuring out the budget for a new tool can feel like a moving target, but desk booking software pricing is usually pretty straightforward. Most companies in this space follow a few common models, so once you know what to look for, you can compare your options and find a plan that fits your needs without any surprise fees. The key is to look beyond the monthly price and consider the total value—like how much time you’ll save and how much more efficiently you’ll be able to use your office space. Let’s break down what you can expect to see. Per-User vs. Per-Desk: Which Pricing Model is Right for You? When you start looking at pricing pages, you’ll notice two main models: per-user or per-desk. Per-user pricing means you pay a set fee for each employee who has access to the software. This is great for companies where most of the team comes into the office regularly, even if they don’t all come in on the same day. Per-desk pricing, on the other hand, charges you based on the number of desks available for booking. This can be a good fit if you have significantly more employees than desks. Most modern tools, including Officely, use a per-user model because it’s simpler to manage as your team grows or shrinks. Typical Pricing: What to Budget For When you start exploring your options, you’ll find that most desk booking tools operate on either a per-user or per-desk model. The per-user model charges a monthly fee for each employee who can access the software, making it a great fit for teams that come into the office regularly. The per-desk model, on the other hand, charges based on the number of desks available for booking. This can be a more economical choice for organizations with a larger workforce than their total number of desks. title: Truth-Driven Development
summary: AI-assisted code generation breaks the key assumption engineering workflows were built on.
body_text: AI-assisted code generation breaks the key assumption engineering workflows were built on. That assumption is code is scarce. Code is now abundant. When code becomes abundant, verification becomes the bottleneck. And when verification becomes the bottleneck, the most valuable artifact in a codebase stops being the code. It becomes the truth . This is the premise of Truth-Driven Development (TrDD): define what must be true, then let implementations come and go. AI makes code easy, and easy changes everything Software development was constrained by the cost of writing code. That constraint forced focus and tradeoffs. It forced people to think carefully about what they built because the build itself was expensive. Now you can produce code faster than humans can review it. You can get Claude or Codex or Devin to generate multiple "reasonable" implementations of the same feature. You can change code constantly without feeling any cost, until something breaks. But this generates variance. Different structures, abstractions, assumptions, and edge cases. That variance is not inherently bad, but it's fatal if you don't have a stable definition of correctness. If you can regenerate the implementation at will, you need something else that stays fixed. The old answer was TDD. TDD's original promise was straightforward: Write a failing test (red). Write code to make it pass (green). Refactor safely (refactor). This intent was solid. Tests act as a forcing function for clarity, and a safety harness for change. But in practice, TDD was slow, brittle, overly coupled to implementation details, and too reliant on developer discipline. So TDD became polarizing. Some loved it. Many abandoned it. DHH declared it dead in 2014 , and most of the industry moved on. Moving on was kind of OK, because testing could afford to be reactive. The rate of change was slow enough for reactive to work. Testing didn't disappear; it just got demoted. It became a second-class citizen in the development workflow: something you added after the fact, something QA handled, something that lived downstream of the "real" engineering work. Code was the artifact. Tests were the chore. That can no longer work. Velocity is too high to manually verify. So we have to shift back to treating testing as the primary constraint on what gets built, which forces a question most teams haven't had to answer clearly: What is your system of truth when code can change faster than you can inspect it? What is TrDD? Truth-Driven Development treats behavior-level tests as the primary artifacts of development and code as disposable output that must satisfy them. The truth comes before the implementation. Here’s an example. You're building authenticated access to a billing page. Traditional workflow: write the auth logic, build the billing UI, then maybe add some tests afterward. TrDD inverts this. Start by defining the behaviors that must be true: "A valid user can sign in and reach the dashboard." "A logged-out user cannot access /billing; they are redirected to /login." "After login, the user can access /billing and sees their plan and invoices." These aren't test cases. They're truths . They describe what should happen, not how. No selectors, no internal architecture. Just outcomes. Now the flow is: Run truth. It fails. /billing is reachable while logged out. That's your red state. You now have an unambiguous definition of "not done." Prompt Claude to fix it. It enforces an auth guard and redirects unauthenticated users. Re-run truth. The redirect passes, but billing content fails because invoices aren't wired up. Prompt again. Claude completes the implementation: billing data call, empty-state handling. Re-run truth. All behaviors pass. Green. Now refactor freely. Let AI reorganize routes, restructure state, and rename components. It doesn't matter what the implementation looks like. The only thing that matters is whether truth holds. Truth stays stable because it validates behavior, not DOM structure or internal architecture. A refactor that changes every file but preserves behavior passes. A one-line change that breaks the auth redirect fails. Release is allowed only if the truth suite passes in CI. Not "someone reviewed the PR." Not "QA spot-checked it." The system ships when truth is satisfied. Six months later, someone rewrites the auth system. If that rewrite breaks the redirect invariant, the failure surfaces in CI before users see it. That's the difference between "we have tests" and "we have truth." We can generalize to this: Define truth (behavior contracts). Use AI to generate implementation. Verify against truth. Refactor or regenerate freely , because truth remains stable. Isn’t this just TDD, with a lowercase r to seem cool? No. Two differences matter. First, abstraction level. TDD as practiced was usually unit-level. Test this function. Mock that dependency. Assert this return value. Those tests were tightly coupled to implementation, which made them brittle and refactoring painful. TrDD operates at the behavior level. It doesn't care how you implement the auth guard. It cares whether a logged-out user can reach /billing. Second, the role tests play. TDD was a developer discipline: a practice you adopted because it led to better design. You could skip it. Many did. TrDD is an operational necessity. When AI generates code faster than you can read it, you don't have the option of "we'll add tests later." Truth is the only thing standing between you and plausible wrongness at scale. Truth is how you keep the system anchored. TDD said: write tests first, and your code will be better. TrDD says: define truth first, or you won't know if your code is right at all. Engineering becomes truth design TrDD does not demand that teams become purists, but does ask teams to accept a new reality: Code can and will change constantly. AI can and will generate plausible wrongness. The only way to move fast without breaking everything is to define correctness as executable truth. TrDD changes what testing means. Testing stops being a phase you move through or a role you hire for. It becomes the governing constraint on the entire system. The test suite is the contract. CI enforces it. Nothing ships unless truth is satisfied. This is not "more testing." It's testing as infrastructure. Just as you wouldn't ship without version control, you don't ship without truth passing. It also changes where humans add value. When AI handles implementation, the human contribution moves upstream: specifying correct behavior, defining invariants, deciding what matters enough to encode as truth. The differentiator is no longer "can you write the code." It's "can you define what must be true, clearly and completely." That's a different skill. It requires precision about behavior, not just familiarity with syntax. Build with truth If you're building with AI, or planning to, you don't need more code generation. You need a better definition of correctness. Momentic helps teams adopt Truth-Driven Development by turning product behaviors into stable, executable truth that keeps up with change. If you want to see what TrDD looks like in your own app, we'd love to show you .

body_text: Staying compliant when moving funds First things first, this example is for a business where one entity owns 100% of the other. There may be multiple subsidiaries, but for simplicity's sake, let’s assume one parent company and one subsidiary. Also, I’m assuming that the parent company holds investment funds and is otherwise not used for anything else (like sales or hiring). All hires, sales contracts, and expenses are in your subsidiary, at least for now. In this situation, you have two options to document the cash transfer (the investment you raised) from your parent company to your operational subsidiary. Remember that each company has its own circumstances to consider, so treat this post as a starting point for your research. Both of these can be applied at the end of your financial year, so don’t panic if you have sent money sporadically without documenting it. 🗒️ Intragroup loan ‍ The parent company transfers money and records it in both accounts as a loan. To comply with tax laws, you must apply an interest rate to the loan so it's “arms-length”. Not doing this could cause issues with tax authorities further down the line. Draft a loan agreement, and you are good to go. Pros‍ Can be repaid, so if you plan to work in your home country now but want to open an office where your parent company is in a year or so, you can send money back without too much complexity. Cons The interest rate will generate income in your parent company, and if you have no plans to repay it, it might create additional admin for you and your accountants. 🗒️ Capital contribution The parent company invests money in the subsidiary. The subsidiary records the cash as capital (equity). Consider this an internal fundraise — the subsidiary can then issue shares in itself to the parent company (even though it’s already 100% owned by the parent). A board resolution and notifying your local company register is how you formalise this. Pros‍ Straightforward, with no ongoing commitments or interest complications. Cons Irreversible, so if you need to return funds back to the parent company, you would have to consider a separate mechanism to move funds back, like dividends or a loan. Services agreements and transfer pricing‍ The two options above can be used when the parent company is simply an investment-taking shell. If you need to transfer funds between two entities with operational activities (R&D and Sales), then you may need a services agreement, and you need to work out the correct transfer pricing method to apply. Just recharging costs can leave you with a tax headache, so you essentially need a mark-up. This also includes cases where one of your companies is used for invoicing (as your customer or supplier might want to deal only with a US company). This is a wholly separate and complex area that I’ll cover in a different post. If you are heading towards your year-end and have made these types of transfers without any documents, don’t worry. Speak to us, and we can set this up for you. Then, get back to building something people want!

title: Hingham Savings Authorizes Stock Repurchase Program
summary: HINGHAM, Mass., Dec. 05, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HINGHAM INSTITUTION FOR SAVINGS (NASDAQ:HIFS) (“the Bank”), Hingham, Massachusetts, announced that its...
body_text: HINGHAM, Mass., Dec. 05, 2025 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HINGHAM INSTITUTION FOR SAVINGS (NASDAQ:HIFS) (“the Bank”), Hingham, Massachusetts, announced that its Board of Directors has authorized a share repurchase program (“the Program”) pursuant to which the Bank may repurchase up to $20 million of its outstanding common stock, having received all regulatory approvals as may be required. Under the Program, repurchases can be made from time to time using a variety of methods, which may include open market purchases, privately negotiated transactions, block trades, or any combination of such methods, in accordance with applicable securities laws and regulations. The Bank regularly evaluates all capital allocation options, in light of the Bank’s capital requirements and the prospective returns on such options, including the incremental return on organic balance sheet growth, investments, dividends (both regular and special), and share repurchases. The Program permits the Bank to repurchase shares when, in the estimate of senior management, the return on share repurchases is attractive relative to alternative capital allocation options. The Program is fundamentally price sensitive and does not obligate the Bank to acquire any shares at all. It may be suspended, modified, or discontinued at any time without prior notice. The Program is authorized through December 6, 2026. The Board anticipates reconsidering the size and terms of the Program on an annual basis, subject to regulatory approval as may be required. Incorporated in 1834, Hingham Institution for Savings is one of America’s oldest banks. The Bank maintains offices in Boston, Nantucket, Washington, D.C., and San Francisco. The Bank’s shares of common stock are listed and traded on The NASDAQ Stock Market under the symbol HIFS. CONTACT: Patrick R. Gaughen, President & Chief Operating Officer (781) 783-1761

title: Five ways to lower network cost of ownership with Inseego
summary: Discover how Inseego's 5G FWA and Inseego Connect™ cloud management eliminate costly installation, maintenance, and downtime to drastically reduce your network TCO.
body_text: Traditional network infrastructure fiber, cable, and even satellite, forces enterprises to accept high initial investment and complex, recurring maintenance. The Inseego 5G ecosystem, centered on devices like the FX4200 5G Cellular Router , MiFi X PRO hotspot , MiFi PRO M4 mobile router , and FW3000 Outdoor CPE , completely disrupts this high-cost model. By leveraging a unified platform of high-performance hardware and the centralized management of Inseego Connect and the Inseego Mobile App , businesses can dramatically reduce their Total Cost of Ownership (TCO). Here is how Inseego’s solutions reduce network TCO. 1) Zero-touch installation and plug-and-play come together The most significant financial benefit of Inseego 5G FWA is the elimination of massive costs associated with civil engineering, trenching, complex wiring, and conduit installation, making it the preferred access choice where wireline is costly or impractical. Inseego’s 5G Cellular Router FWA line: The instant infrastructure replacement or deployment The FX4200 is designed for a "better than plug-and-play" experience, ensuring that large rollouts for retail or branch offices can be handled quickly by existing personnel, resulting in significant cost savings upfront and overtime. Zero-Touch Provisioning (ZTP) : Upon its first boot, all Inseego devices automatically authenticate with Inseego Connect™ and apply pre-defined templates, firmware, and security policies. Intuitive on-the-go setup: The FX4200 features a display screen that offers signal information and includes a battery backup. This allows staff to walk around with the device and position the router for the best signal and connect it "on the go," without needing hardwired power or advanced testing tools during the initial setup phase. Close-up of the Inseego 5G Cellular Router FX4200 built-in display Major initial cost savings: The intuitive setup and ZTP functionality eliminate the need to hire expensive, highly specialized network technicians for installation. Existing on-site personnel can handle large-scale rollouts, accelerate the time-to-market and minimizing the initial costs associated with complex integration and specialized labor. High-performance 5G: Not only that, Inseego’s latest 5G cellular router, the FX4200, is built on Qualcomm Dragonwing FWA Gen 3. This means it delivers high-performance 5G (multi-gigabit speeds and low latency) that is instantly ready to support demanding applications like voice, video, and cloud services right out of the box. Unlock lightning-fast 5G internet almost anywhere 2) Take advantage of easy device management with cloud software Long-term TCO is dominated by ongoing operational costs. The centralized management provided by Inseego Connect and the Inseego Mobile App is specifically engineered to minimize recurring costs by automating maintenance and eliminating expensive site visits with remote management. Inseego Connect: The zero-truck-roll platform Inseego Connect is the cloud-based platform that allows IT teams to manage geographically dispersed devices, from FX4200 routers to MiFi X PRO hotspots, from a single, unified management dashboard or mobile app. This centralized visibility and control translates directly into massive savings and efficiency gains. Inseego Connect & Inseego Mobile App Remote maintenance & management: This platform provides full-featured remote management at scale, allowing IT teams to configure settings, view diagnostics, run speed tests, view speed test history, push firmware, and manage updates remotely. By enabling bulk actions (applying configuration templates, editing failover policies) and providing a single cloud platform for every FX4200 and MiFi node, IT teams gain full control "without needing to dispatch a field technician to troubleshoot issues." The Inseego FWA router provides a secure, alternate management path for other routers and switches through remote out-of-band-management. IT teams can securely tunnel through to remotely access and troubleshoot the console terminal of a downed device. Preventive operational cost control: Proactive health analytics: Automated alerts and threshold-based notifications prevent costly downtime. IT teams are alerted to potential issues before they cause slowdowns or trigger unexpected bandwidth overages, allowing for immediate remote correction. Remote diagnostic terminal: This powerful tool allows network administrators to run network diagnostic commands remotely from within Inseego Connect. This means IT teams have the capability to debug complex issues, run ping tests, or traceroute without relying on time-consuming on-site reporting or dispatching a technician. Centralized visibility: IT teams can view network topology, device inventory, and real-time diagnostics (signal strength, throughput, speed tests, and data usage), enabling swift, remote issue resolution without relying on time-consuming on-site reporting. Logistical & security savings: GPS asset management: For businesses utilizing portable MiFi X PRO hotspots or the MiFi PRO M4, Inseego Connect offers geo-fencing and GPS asset tracking. This capability improves inventory control and reduces the operational expenditure and risk associated with asset loss and complex auditing processes. Policy enforcement and auditing: Policy controls, such as scheduling updates, enforcing network rules, and reviewing change logs for governance, reduce administrative overhead. Built-in security (IPSec VPN, encrypted tunnels, role-based access) minimizes the cost and risk associated with data breaches and compliance failures. Real-world savings with Inseego Connect: The Tractor Supply case study A major U.S. retailer, Tractor Supply, demonstrated massive, long-term operational savings by deploying Inseego's solution across over 2,200 retail locations. This large-scale rollout leveraged Inseego Connect's ability to deliver seamless remote configuratio n and management. Inseego Connect allowed Tractor Supply to quickly and efficiently deploy, activate, and manage all network settings and policies across thousands of devices without needing to send personnel to each store. This capability significantly reduced the need for costly on-site field technicians and minimized "truck rolls" across the entire fleet, resulting in substantial, quantifiable savings during their product rollout. Further management cost reduction with the Inseego Mobile App The Inseego Mobile App is a vital tool for reducing operational costs by shifting basic technical support away from the central IT helpdesk and onto the end-user's device. Inseego Mobile App with Inseego products on display Minimizing helpdesk labor costs: The app empowers end-users to perform basic, first-line troubleshooting for their devices (like the FX3100 and MiFi X PRO). By guiding users through self-service steps, such as confirming wireless coverage, ensuring the SIM card is inserted correctly, or correctly restarting the device, the app prevents a high volume of Level 1 support tickets. Preventing unnecessary truck rolls: Beyond the helpdesk, the app helps avoid costly dispatches of field technicians. It provides users with intuitive diagnostics and signal placement assistance, allowing them to resolve common connectivity issues like poor signal strength due to their device placement. Full remote management: The Inseego Mobile App acts as a convenient, portable management console, enabling IT administrators to remotely manage all their Inseego devices from a smartphone or tablet as long as the devices are registered with Inseego Connect. This allows for quick, on-the-go checks of device status, remote reboots, and viewing critical diagnostics. Optimizing device installation: For new deployments, the app often includes features that simplify initial setup, such as visual guides for optimal placement and antenna alignment, further reducing the need for specialized installers and associated initial costs. 3) Mitigating costly downtime with automatic failover Powerful connectivity is essential for TCO because downtime is catastrophic. Inseego mitigates the significant financial impact of interruptions through built-in resilience and automated failover capabilities, ensuring consistent business operations. Layered failover options: Many of Inseego’s devices support Dual WAN capabilities, allowing the device to act as a wireless failover for a primary wired connection (like fiber or cable). If the wireline network goes down, the Inseego 5G FWA solution instantly takes over, maintaining connectivity and avoiding the high costs of a complete network outage. Inseego Connect also triggers all related failover alarms and threshold-based notifications, so admins can react immediately. Auto-SIM Select: This feature (on devices like the FX4200) automates the SIM select process by allowing the device to run a speed test on boot-up for each installed SIM card. It then autonomously selects the SIM and carrier that provides the best connectivity and throughput, ensuring optimal performance and enabling hands-off switching. Ruggedized resilience: Outdoor units like the FW3000 are engineered for physical resilience, featuring an IP67 rating against dust and water ingress and a wide operating temperature range (e.g., 22°F to 158°F). This rugged design prevents device failure due to environmental exposure, reducing emergency replacement and service downtime. 4) Enabling connectivity where it’s challenging Inseego 5G FWA is often a superior and more cost-effective choice than traditional infrastructure in environments that are underserved or unserved by wired solutions. Long-range, high-speed access: The FW3000 Outdoor CPE series is a robust, all-in-one solution that combines multiple high-gain directional antennas with routing capabilities. This device can sustain 5G speeds up to 10 km away from a cell tower, ensuring high-speed access even in remote or underserved locations. Cost-effective indoor coverage: Extending 5G coverage indoors is simpler and more cost-effective with the FW3000 Outdoor CPE. The FW3000 maximizes external signal acquisition and brings the connection inside using a single Ethernet cable that delivers both data and power (PoE), eliminating the need for expensive dedicated wiring or specialized installers and thereby significantly reducing the cost and complexity of internal architecture. 5) 5G Advanced architecture: Preventing future costs with AI and slicing As the 5G standard evolves toward 5G Advanced (3GPP Release 18+), Inseego is ready to integrate new 5G capabilities that drive cost reduction through enhanced resilience, resource sharing, and efficiency. Network Slicing and Resource Optimization Network slicing, enabled by technologies like Network Function Virtualization (NFV) and Software-Defined Networking (SDN), fundamentally reduces initial costs and operational costs by allowing multiple logical networks to share a single physical infrastructure. Reduced costs through traffic isolation: Inseego already supports basic network slicing features on its 5G FWA devices. Slicing improves operational efficiency by leveraging inherent isolation and advanced automation functions. This reduces the need for manual intervention by network engineers. This flexibility enables providers to offer tailored services (e.g., Ultra Reliable Low Latency Communications (URLLC) or enhanced Mobile Broadband (eMBB)) optimized for specific customer needs. The future of efficiency: 5G Advanced and AI integration The move toward 5G Advanced (5G-A) focuses heavily on driving down operational costs through integrated intelligence, energy efficiency, and enhanced automation. By supporting the foundational architecture for 5G-A, Inseego hardware protects your TCO against future obsolescence. AI for dynamic cost reduction: A core feature of 5G-A is the deep integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML). This intelligence is used to automate complex, real-time tasks like energy efficiency control, dynamic traffic steering, and predictive maintenance. These automated processes minimize the necessity for costly, manual intervention by network engineers, assuring a continuous reduction in operational costs. Massive energy savings and sustainability: The 5G Advanced framework focuses heavily on network energy savings and sustainability. Since power is a significant portion of long-term operational costs, AI/ML models can dynamically switch components to sleep states or optimize power consumption based on real-time traffic load. This translates directly into substantial, measurable cost reduction through lower utility bills. Proactive network self-healing: AI enables the network to become proactive and self-healing. By analyzing massive streams of diagnostic data, AI can predict potential hardware failures or service degradation before it impacts users. This shift from reactive troubleshooting to predictive maintenance eliminates expensive, emergency field technician dispatches and prevents unexpected downtime costs. Inseego aims to reduce the TCO of your network By combining powerful 5G hardware (FX4200, FX3100, FW3000, MiFi X PRO, MiFi PRO M4) with intelligent, centralized software (Inseego Connect and Mobile App), and building in support for future 5G advancements and resource optimization features, Inseego provides an ecosystem that fundamentally lowers TCO.
